So today we start a series on the entirety of human history. We'll be going very fast, and what's important is for you to understand the concepts. So if there are ideas you don't understand, it's very important that you raise your hand, challenge me, and ask for clarification. We start off with the dawn of humanity. Charles Darwin is arguably the most influential thinker of the past 200 years because he wrote a book called *On the Origin of Species* and presented us with the theory of evolution. You all know this theory because it's taught in school and embedded in our everyday lives.

And there are three main ideas to the theory of evolution: first, that it was accidental—genetic mutations leading to survival; second, it is materialistic, meaning everything you can see is what exists; and third, it is emergent, a bottom-up process. The fear of evolution marked a turning point in human history because before this, European countries were Christian, believing that there was a divine God who created us and as such we were all equal before the eyes of God. Therefore, you cannot enslave or kill other people.

The three main ideas of Christianity are: first, one omniscient and omnipresent God; the spirit, the Holy Spirit, infuses life with meaning and purpose; the world is a mystery, holding faith in things we cannot understand; and God has a plan that is mysterious. The theory of evolution destroys this concept of the universe and introduces a more materialistic one.

This happened for three reasons: first, Europeans were engaged in imperialism in the 19th century, conquering other people, colonizing them, and essentially committing genocide. They needed a theory to explain why they were doing this, and Darwin's theory of "survival of the fittest" was the most appropriate. The idea is that the world is divided into races, with the white race being superior, thus having legitimacy in colonizing other people. Evolution would give rise to racism and eugenics.

Before Darwinism, we didn't really have a concept of race because everyone was equal in the eyes of God. Now, with the rise of Darwinism, the world is divided according to race as well. Because of evolution theory, people started believing in eugenics—the idea that stupid people should be sterilized to avoid diluting the genetic pool.

Even today, there are still many who believe in racism and eugenics. The thing about evolution is that it's a theology—a theory of human progress. Even though evolution thinks genetic mutation is an accident, the theology suggests that the strong survive, which makes might right. In many ways, evolution is a rejection of Christianity.

So you would think that Christians would oppose Darwinism and evolutionary theory. But surprisingly, when the book came out in 1859, by 1879, the theory of evolution had dominated the entire Western world. It became the dominant idea in schools, universities, and sciences.
